title: Your NRI Streaming Guide — The Best of This Week's OTT Drops (May 18-24)
excerpt: From a reality show about Indian expats in Dubai to a prestige courtroom drama, here's what to queue up on Netflix, Prime Video, ZEE5, and SonyLIV this week — all available internationally.
body:
Your couch. A cup of chai. A subscription you're already paying for. Let's make the most of all three this week.

Here's what's dropping on OTT platforms between May 18-24 that's actually worth your time — sorted by how urgently you need to clear your evening schedule.

## 🔥 The Must-Watch: Desi Bling (Netflix, May 20)

If you're an NRI, this show was literally made about your life — or at least the Dubai version of it. **Desi Bling** is Netflix's new reality series following Indian expats living their most glamorous lives in the UAE, and the cast is stacked: **Karan Kundrra** and **Tejasswi Prakash** bring their massive fanbases, while the show promises the kind of personal drama, social dynamics, and unfiltered desi energy that made *Fabulous Lives of Bollywood Wives* a guilty-pleasure phenomenon.

The hook for diaspora audiences is obvious — this is a show about Indians who left India, navigating identity and ambition in a foreign land. Sound familiar? Whether you're in Dubai, Dallas, or Dundee, there's something here that'll hit close to home.

**Where to watch:** Netflix (available globally)

## ⚖️ The Prestige Pick: System (Amazon Prime Video, May 22)

Director **Ashwiny Iyer Tiwari** (*Bareilly Ki Barfi*, *Panga*) enters the courtroom with **System**, a legal drama that pairs two powerhouse actresses: **Sonakshi Sinha** as a public prosecutor and **Jyotika** as opposing counsel. This isn't your typical Bollywood courtroom shouting match — early reviews suggest a character study wrapped in legal procedure, closer to *Shahid* than *Jolly LLB*.

The Sonakshi-Jyotika matchup alone is worth the price of admission. Two generations of leading ladies going head-to-head in a genre that Hindi cinema rarely gets right? Sign us up.

**Where to watch:** Amazon Prime Video (available in US, UK, Canada, Australia, and most international markets)

## 🗡️ The Dark Horse: Satrangi: Badle Ka Khel (ZEE5, May 22)

Don't sleep on this one. **Satrangi** is a revenge drama set in rural Uttar Pradesh starring **Anshumaan Pushkar**, and it digs into caste, identity, and power dynamics with the kind of raw intensity that OTT has made possible. This is the stuff that would never get a theatrical release but thrives in the streaming ecosystem — dark, unflinching, and deeply rooted in the Indian heartland.

**Where to watch:** ZEE5 (global app available — works in US, UK, Canada, Australia, and 190+ countries)

## 💕 The Light One: Madhuvidhu (SonyLIV, May 22)

Need something lighter after all that intensity? **Madhuvidhu** is a Malayalam romantic comedy led by **Sharafudheen**, built around family superstition and marriage chaos. If you've ever had a relative consult a jyotish before approving your partner, this one will feel uncomfortably relatable. Malayalam comedies have been on a tear lately, and this looks like it continues the streak.

**Where to watch:** SonyLIV (global app available in US, UK, Canada, Middle East, and more)

## 🌍 Also on the Radar (Non-Desi but Good)

- **Ladies First** (Netflix, May 22) — Sacha Baron Cohen's new comedy. If *Borat* energy is your thing, keep an eye on this.
- **Jack Ryan: Ghost War** (Amazon Prime Video, May 20) — The spy franchise continues. Solid background-viewing material.
- **The Boroughs** (Netflix, May 21) — From the Duffer Brothers (*Stranger Things*). Horror-adjacent, community-driven storytelling.

## The Verdict

This is a genuinely strong week for desi OTT. **Desi Bling** is the conversation-starter (your WhatsApp groups will be buzzing), **System** is the quality pick for serious cinema lovers, and **Satrangi** is the dark horse that could surprise everyone.

The best part? All four major platforms — Netflix, Prime Video, ZEE5, and SonyLIV — have robust international apps. No VPN gymnastics required. Whether you're streaming from San Francisco, London, Toronto, or Melbourne, everything on this list is accessible.

Queue it up. Chai optional but recommended. ☕

*Dates confirmed as of May 19, 2026. Streaming availability may vary by region — check your local platform for confirmation.*
